ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding any verifier, director, shareholder, settlor, accounting officer or authorized signatory, the law firm must screen against (i) the New Zealand Police Terrorist Watch List and sanctions maintained by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade under the Sanctions Act 2020; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Lists; (iii) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists to protect USD clearing and correspondent banking; and (iv) a commercial PEP database. PEP status includes foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs and international-organization PEPs as defined in the AML/CFT Act 2009; enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth documentation and senior-management approval are required for any PEP, close associate, or red-flag hit. Screening must be repeated at frequent intervals during onboarding and before any IP assignment, share transfer, dividend payment or loan transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register (Companies Office Online Services at register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must use Latin-script letters A-Z, Arabic numerals and permitted punctuation; Chinese and non-Latin characters are not accepted in the registered legal name. Where a non-English brand is intended, a phonetic English transliteration must be registered as the official name, and any foreign-script usage remains a trading name only. The Companies Office applies a four-tier naming classification: (1) wholly descriptive or generic names are refused; (2) distinctive invented or arbitrary names are accepted; (3) descriptive or geographic names with a distinctive element are accepted only when not misleading; and (4) names containing sensitive or prohibited tokens require prior approval from the responsible regulator or Minister.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Request an extension or renewal before expiration by logging into the Companies Office name approval dashboard and re-running the name reservation search; a renewal fee applies. If the Registrar rejects a name, file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies within 20 working days, attaching evidence of distinguishability, consent from any regulator for sensitive tokens, and a fresh transliteration certificate. The Registrar must issue a determinative response; if the refusal is upheld, the applicant may appeal to the High Court under the Companies Act 1993 name-adjudication provisions or immediately submit a corrected name application with a new reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are accepted as a statutory registered office under the Companies Act 1993 because the Act requires only a physical address in New Zealand for service of process; however, the Inland Revenue Department will not treat a virtual mailbox as a place of business for GST or income-tax commercial-substance analysis, and NZ banks will generally reject a virtual-office-only address for merchant settlement accounts or corporate accounts in the interactive AI pet robot hardware industry unless the entity also provides a local operational site, warehouse, stock-holding arrangement or agent. Therefore a virtual office is permissible only as a compliance address and is not a substitute for commercial substance; it will likely be rejected for substantive tax and banking purposes if the company is purely shell.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) registered office differs from actual operational premises; (2) no employees or sublease agreement; (3) GST registration with no operating asset; (4) repeated refunds or zero declared income; (5) non-resident director; and (6) virtual-mailbox address on invoices. Quantified risk: 15-25% annual probability of an unannounced IRD or Companies Office inspection for a virtual-office-only non-resident-owned company, increasing to 40% if GST refunds are claimed or a listed director triggers a high-wealth or AML red-flag profile.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (1993 No 105) of New Zealand, as amended, including sections 10 (constitution), 12-15 (incorporation requirements), 16-19 (company names), 20 (certificate of incorporation), 41-48 (share capital and issue of shares), 87 (share certificates), 128-149 (director duties), 159-180 (meetings and resolutions), 188-190 (registered office and address for service), 194-196 (changes to director details), 200 and 202-204 (officer appointments), and 254-265 (records, registers and accounting documents).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZ1 - Application for Incorporation of a Company, filed online through the New Zealand Companies Office RealMe service
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Companies Act 1993 does not impose a minimum paid-up capital requirement on a company limited by shares, and no escrow or blocked capital account is required or permitted to be filed at the New Zealand Companies Office. Shares may be issued with no par value, and initial shares may be allotted for such consideration as the directors determine in accordance with section 41 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE COMPANY WHEREAS: A. The subscriber has caused this company, being the Company, to be incorporated under the Companies Act 1993, a certificate of incorporation having been issued by the Registrar of Companies. B. The first directors have consented to act as statutory officers of the Company. C. The Company has adopted a constitution dated the date of incorporation. D. The board desires to record the formal receipt of incorporation, to establish the Company financial banking mandate, to fix its registered office, and to appoint its statutory officers. NOW IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. ADOPTION OF INCORPORATION AND CONSTITUTION: That the certificate of incorporation dated 2025 and the constitution of the Company, as filed with the Registrar of Companies, are hereby received, approved, adopted and ratified, and the directors are authorized to issue share certificates as required by section 87 of the Companies Act 1993. 2. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT OF SHARES: That the shares of the Company be designated as ordinary shares with no par value, and the subscribers and initial shareholders be and hereby subscribe for the number of shares set out opposite their names in the register of shareholders. The board accepts the subscriptions and allotments and directs the entry of such allotments in the share register. No shares shall be issued for a consideration that is less than nil; the full issue consideration, if any, will be applied to working capital. Since New Zealand does not require minimum paid-up capital or a blocked capital account, no escrow arrangement is required. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE AND ADDRESS FOR SERVICE: That the registered office of the Company shall be at 123 Queen Street, Auckland, New Zealand, and the address for service shall be the same. The board directs that every notice, process or communication permitted to be delivered to the Company shall be delivered to that office. Any agent or person lawfully in possession of the office is authorized to accept service on behalf of the Company. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: That the directors be and are hereby jointly authorized, subject to internal treasury limits, to open, maintain, close and operate banking facilities with the company bank, including checking, savings and foreign currency accounts in New Zealand dollars and United States dollars. The board designates the Managing Director and the Company Secretary as the two authorized account signatories. The mandate shall require joint signatures for all transactions exceeding NZD 100,000 and single signatures for smaller transactions. 5. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: That the following persons be and are hereby appointed as statutory officers of the Company with effect from the date of this resolution: the Managing Director, the Director and Board Chairperson, and the Company Secretary, with full responsibility for minutes, statutory registers and filings. Each officer has the powers, duties and authorities granted by the Companies Act 1993 and the constitution. 6. BORROWING POWERS AND GENERAL AUTHORITY: That the directors be and are hereby authorized to exercise all borrowing powers of the Company, to grant security, to execute deeds and documents, and to do all things necessary to carry out the foregoing resolutions. 7. RECORDS AND SEAL: That this resolution be recorded in the minutes, that the certificate of incorporation be kept in the statutory register, and that the common seal, if any, be adopted. CERTIFIED that the foregoing is a true extract of the minutes of the first meeting of the board of directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name availability search and corporate governance setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register online name search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before any statutory filing, the incorporator must conduct a name availability search on the New Zealand Companies Office website and lodge an online name query. The company name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing name and must not include restricted words such as bank or trust unless separate authorization is obtained from the relevant regulator. The draft constitution must comply with section 10 of the Companies Act 1993 and must state the company name, registered office, share structure and restrictions on director authority. Confirm each director and shareholder has provided a signed consent to act, and confirm the proposed registered office is a physical street address in New Zealand capable of receiving legal documents. No notarization is required for the online application, but original consents must be retained in the statutory records. This step prevents later rejection of the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and primary business description
Proposed physical New Zealand registered office address
Full legal names, residential addresses and dates of birth of each initial director and shareholder
Signed consents of each director and shareholder
Draft constitution of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is withheld or queried, file a new name expression or apply to the Registrar for special permission; resubmit on the same portal with corrected wording within 15 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the Form NZ1 application for incorporation to the Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office online services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the New Zealand Companies Office online portal using RealMe and select the service to register a new company. Complete the electronic application for incorporation, inputting the approved company name, registered office, address for service, full names and residential addresses of directors and shareholders, and the exact share allotment. Attach the signed constitution and director and shareholder consents. The application must be authorized by each subscriber through the authentication method provided by the portal. There is no requirement for capital escrow, share capital deposit or notarization; however, supporting identity documents may be requested electronically. Pay the prescribed fee electronically and submit the Form NZ1. The Registrar will review the application, and once satisfied, issue the certificate of incorporation in pdf form and record the company on the Companies Register. The lodgement receipt and certificate should be saved permanently.
required_dossiers: Form NZ1 - Application for Incorporation of a Company
Signed constitution of the company
Signed consent to act as director for each proposed director
Signed consent or authorization of each subscriber and shareholder
Physical registered office address and confirmation from the registered office service, if used
Identification documents of directors if requested by the Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or correction request, amend the electronic application within 20 business days and resubmit the corrected pages. If the application is rejected, the same filing fee payment can be applied to a revised application submitted within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation governance: adopt first board resolution, issue shares and approve banking mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors and company secretary of the New Zealand company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after receiving the certificate of incorporation, convene the first board of directors meeting, which may be held as a written resolution signed by all directors under section 180 of the Companies Act 1993. The board must adopt the pro-forma first board resolution set out in the legal framework, including formal acceptance of incorporation, allotment of the initial ordinary shares to the named subscribers, and issue of share certificates. The board must also approve the company bank mandate, appoint the statutory officers, and instruct the registered office service or agent to accept service of documents. All statutory records, including the share register, director register, minute book and certificate of incorporation, must be kept at the registered office in accordance with sections 189 and 254 of the Companies Act 1993. Execute any banking mandate forms using the signatures authorized in the board resolution and submit them to the financial institution.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation issued by the Companies Office
Fully executed first board resolution
Initial share register and signed share certificates
Signed consent to act as managing director, board chairperson and company secretary
Minute book and common seal, if adopted
Banking mandate form with authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the mandate or any officer refuses to serve, adopt a supplementary board resolution to correct the mandates and file any change in director details with the Companies Office within 20 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration with the Inland Revenue Department and GST or PAYE enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a myIR account and apply to the Inland Revenue Department for the company IRD number using the online new company registration service. State the primary business activity as ISIC 3240 - manufacture of games and toys, and provide the expected date of business commencement. Register for Goods and Services Tax if taxable supplies will exceed NZD 60,000 in any consecutive twelve month period, or voluntarily when the company wishes to claim GST input tax credits. If the company will employ staff, register for PAYE and employer obligations at the same time. The IRD number is required for banking, customs clearance and supplier onboarding, so the application should be completed before issuing the first invoice. The application includes identity verification steps; answer all business ownership and banking questions accurately and attach the certificate of incorporation if requested.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
Company constitution, if requested by IRD
Company registered office and communication address
Primary business activity and ISIC code
Expected annual turnover and GST registration decision
Bank account details of the New Zealand company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number is delayed, contact the IRD Business Tax contact centre and provide the application reference; IRD will normally resolve identity and registration queries within 10 working days after receiving supplementary evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, building, fire and environmental compliance for the manufacturing and assembly site
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local territorial authority building consent authority, WorkSafe New Zealand, and Fire and Emergency New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before operating the assembly line for the interactive AI pet robot, obtain or verify the territorial authority building consent and code compliance certificate for the manufacturing premises; the fitout, mezzanine, fire exits, electrical installations and storage racks must meet the Building Act 2004 performance standards. If the site is zoned industrial and the manufacturing activity meets permitted activity standards under the district plan, no resource consent is required; however, if the activity will emit smoke, dust, fumes, trade wastewater, excessive noise, or store hazardous substances, file a resource consent application with the local council and prepare an Assessment of Environmental Effects. Register the company as a PCBU under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 and prepare a written workplace safety plan. Apply to Fire and Emergency New Zealand for approval of a fire evacuation scheme if more than ten employees or visitors may be present. If storing lithium-ion batteries, adhesives or chemicals above the trigger quantities under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996, obtain an HSNO location compliance certificate and provide a hazardous substances inventory.
required_dossiers: Building consent application and structural and fire design drawings
Code compliance certificate or existing building warrant of fitness
Fire evacuation scheme application to Fire and Emergency New Zealand
WorkSafe health and safety operational plan and hazard register
Hazardous substances inventory, safety data sheets and HSNO location compliance evidence
Trade waste consent application to the local council, if process wastewater will be discharged
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If building consent is refused, revise the drawings and resubmit the amended application; if the fire evacuation scheme is rejected, engage a qualified fire consultant to correct the evacuation procedures; if HSNO or resource consent compliance is required, isolate or reduce the quantity of hazardous substances below thresholds or file an application for a limited notified consent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Territorial authority building consent department, WorkSafe New Zealand, Fire and Emergency New Zealand, and the local council administering the Resource Management Act 1991
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No single national industrial manufacturing license is required for ISIC 3240 toy and game assembly; mandatory operating authorization is obtained through Building Code Compliance Certification, Fire Evacuation Scheme Approval under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand (Fire Safety, Fire Evacuation Procedures and Evacuation Schemes) Regulations 2018, WorkSafe Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 compliance, and any district plan resource consent for land use or industrial discharge.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand and the applicable territorial authority council under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt or Permitted Activity - no full Environmental Impact Assessment is required for standard indoor assembly and warehousing of robotics toys when the site complies with the permitted activity noise, dust, traffic and hazardous substance standards of the local district plan. If the activity involves discharge to land or water, large-scale hazardous substance storage, or significant building redevelopment, a resource consent and an Assessment of Environmental Effects will be required under the Resource Management Act 1991 and the local council planning rules.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Trade wastewater discharged to municipal sewer must meet the local council trade waste consent standards, generally including pH 6.0 to 9.0, biological oxygen demand not exceeding 300 mg/L, total suspended solids not exceeding 350 mg/L, and oil and grease not exceeding 50 mg/L; no hazardous waste or untreated process wastewater may enter stormwater drains. Volatile organic compound emissions from adhesives, paints and plastic finishing must not cause noxious, offensive or objectionable odour at or beyond the property boundary under the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Air Quality) Regulations 2004. Hazardous wastes, including rejected lithium-ion battery cells and electronic components, must be stored in bunded impermeable containment holding at least 110 percent of the largest container volume, labeled, inventoried, and transported only by a licensed waste contractor under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is mandatory under the Building Act 2004, requiring compliant means of escape, fire exits, extinguishers, alarms and a building warrant of fitness issued by the territorial authority. Fire and Emergency New Zealand must approve a fire evacuation scheme when payroll or visitor numbers exceed the thresholds in the Fire and Emergency New Zealand (Fire Safety, Fire Evacuation Procedures and Evacuation Schemes) Regulations 2018. Structural load inspections for mezzanine floors and storage racking are required as part of building code compliance. Workplace safety approval under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 requires a written worker participation system, hazard identification, emergency response plans, electrical safety testing of assembly equipment, and a documented health and safety management system accepted by WorkSafe New Zealand.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Tāke) — online portal: myIR at https://myir.ird.govt.nz; general information at https://www.ird.govt.nz. Entity incorporation is separately administered by the New Zealand Companies Office at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz, which issues the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a New Zealand-incorporated limited company with non-resident ownership (foreign-owned NZ Ltd): Step 1 — Incorporate the company with the Companies Office; the incorporation data is automatically shared with Inland Revenue, which allocates the company's 9-digit IRD number. If the IRD number is not issued automatically, file Form IR596 (Application for an IRD Number – Company) through myIR or by post. Step 2 — Provide IRD with the company's registered office address, directors' details, and the foreign parent/beneficial owner's foreign tax identification number (if any) to complete customer due diligence. Step 3 — Register for GST via myIR (or Form IR356) after the IRD number is active. GST registration is compulsory if the company carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand and its taxable supplies in any 12-month period equal or exceed NZD 60,000; exports of goods count as taxable supplies for this threshold even when zero-rated. Voluntary registration below NZD 60,000 is permitted to recover input tax. Step 4 — Set the GST filing frequency (monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly), add the company's bank and foreign-currency settlement accounts (Stripe/credit-card payouts), and nominate a tax agent if applicable. Step 5 — If the company also supplies remote services to New Zealand consumers, assess whether the offshore supplier GST registration regime under sections 8(4A)–(4E) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 applies separately.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation | Territorial_Scope (worldwide income with statutory foreign income exemption) | Tax_Exempt_Zone Not_Applicable — An NZ-incorporated limited company is a New Zealand tax resident and is taxed at the entity level at the standard corporate rate of 28% on worldwide income (Income Tax Act 2007). The foreign income exemption may apply to certain active foreign business income, foreign dividends, and Australian FIF interests. New Zealand has no sub-national corporate income tax and no tax-exempt production zones; the GST is national (has_sub_tax_distinction = false). A US-style pass-through default is not available; the look-through company (LTC) election is restricted to qualifying closely held companies and does not apply to a standard trading company without an affirmative election.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a check-the-box regime; entity classification is statutory. Available elections and mechanisms include: (1) Look-through company (LTC) election under subpart HB (Income Tax Act 2007) for eligible companies with five or fewer owners who are individuals or trustees — income, gains, expenses, and tax credits flow through to owners if elected; not available to a company with corporate shareholders or widely held ownership. (2) Consolidated group election under Part IS for companies under 100% common ownership, allowing a wholly-owned group of companies to file as one consolidated taxpayer. (3) Voluntary GST registration under section 51(4) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 to claim input tax credits before the NZD 60,000 compulsory threshold is reached. (4) Elections and ordering rules under subpart FH for hybrid mismatch arrangements (including the same-jurisdiction election and the imported mismatch timing rules), aligning the NZ result with OECD BEPS Action 2. The Qualifying Company regime is closed to newly incorporated companies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — value-added tax administered under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 — compulsory registration applies to any person carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand whose total value of taxable supplies (including zero-rated exports) in any 12-month period exceeds NZD 60,000, or which is expected to exceed NZD 60,000 in the next 12 months. Voluntary registration is available below the threshold. Non-resident suppliers of remote services and low-value goods to New Zealand consumers are subject to a separate offshore supplier registration regime with the same NZD 60,000 threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based invoice pre-approval. E-invoicing is voluntary for B2B supplies and is implemented on the Peppol framework; government agencies are required to receive Peppol e-invoices but suppliers face no e-invoice mandate. GST-registered businesses must file GST returns electronically via myIR, and the system operates on document-based self-assessment. A tax invoice satisfying section 24 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 must be issued within 28 days of the time of supply, and a buyer must hold a valid tax invoice to claim input tax credits. All records supporting GST returns, including export documentation, must be retained for 7 years under section 22 of the Tax Administration Act 1994.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: A supply of goods is zero-rated under section 11(1)(a) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply (earliest of invoice date, payment date, or goods removal date). The interactive AI pet robots must physically leave New Zealand to a foreign destination and must not be re-imported for use in New Zealand. Services: Zero-rating applies under section 11(1)(d) to services supplied in connection with movable personal property located outside New Zealand, under section 11(1)(e) to services performed outside New Zealand for a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of performance, and under section 11(1)(m) to remote services supplied to a non-resident recipient outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed. Over-the-air software updates and speech-synthesizer cloud services sold separately to overseas customers may qualify as zero-rated remote services if the recipient is a non-resident and the services are performed outside New Zealand. All zero-rated exports must be disclosed in the GST return at 0% and count toward the NZD 60,000 registration threshold.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged electronically with the New Zealand Customs Service via the Trade Single Window / CusMod export entry system for each consignment
Bill of Lading / Sea Waybill / Air Waybill evidencing physical export from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply
Commercial Invoice and GST Tax Invoice (section 24 compliant) issued to the foreign purchaser
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/Stripe payout statement evidencing receipt of foreign-currency proceeds from the overseas buyer
Packing List, HS classification and certificate of origin records for ISIC 3240 / HS 9503 robotic toy hardware
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: New Zealand law imposes no statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark is applied as the schema-default financial covenant. Inland Revenue and the New Zealand Customs Service share data to challenge zero-rating claims where goods are not exported within 28 days, where the exporter fails to hold the required export evidence, or where proceeds are not received from the stated foreign buyer. If the zero-rating claim is incorrect, output tax becomes payable at 15% together with use-of-money interest under section 120 of the Tax Administration Act 1994. Shortfall penalties under section 141 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply by reference to the taxpayer's conduct: 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. Criminal liability under sections 143 and 144 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 exposes directors to fines of up to NZD 50,000 for a first offence and NZD 100,000 for subsequent offences, and imprisonment of up to 5 years for wilful evasion. The general anti-avoidance rule in section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 may be invoked to re-characterise artificial export, pricing, or repatriation arrangements. Standard GST assessments may be amended within 4 years of the end of the return period, extended to 7 years where evasion or fraudulent intent is established; reversed refunds attract use-of-money interest until repaid.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua); prudential supervision and payment system oversight sit with the Reserve Bank, while certain cross-border financial transaction reporting obligations are administered by the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit and the New Zealand Customs Service.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully convertible currency under a free-floating exchange rate regime. There are no exchange controls, no restrictions on capital account transactions, and no requirement for Central Bank approval for foreign direct investment, dividend repatriation, or the conversion of New Zealand dollars to foreign currency. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely transferable both domestically and internationally, subject only to standard AML/CFT reporting thresholds and sanctions screening. Profit remittances by a non-resident shareholder of a New Zealand Limited Company are taxed under the non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) regime, but there is no FX-based blockage or convertibility hurdle.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Exporters may retain foreign currency receipts in offshore or onshore foreign-currency-denominated bank accounts indefinitely. All export proceeds must be reported for statistical balance-of-payments purposes through the standard banking system where a transaction exceeds the AML/CFT threshold, but no repatriation timeline or conversion requirement applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) are not locally regulated as banks in New Zealand. A FinTech EMI holding a European e-money license or an Australian AFSL/ADV may provide foreign-currency payment cards and virtual IBANs, but such providers generally do not offer New Zealand domestic clearing (via the Settlement Account System and Bulk Electronic Clearing System) unless they establish a local arrangement with a New Zealand registered bank. Legal constraints include the prohibition on using the term 'bank' without Reserve Bank registration under the Banking (Preregistration) Act 1980, the requirement for any non-bank payment provider to comply with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act) if it is a 'financial institution' providing money transfer services, and the inability of an offshore EMI to be a direct participant in the New Zealand Payments Net. For a low-risk AI toy hardware exporter, an offshore EMI is viable only for ancillary collection of small international card receipts, not for treasury-grade clearing of trade settlements, which should be routed through a local Tier 1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Non-resident directors of a New Zealand Limited Company may open a corporate bank account remotely, provided the company has a New Zealand registered office and local director, or a local agent with authority. New Zealand banks apply a risk-based approach under the AML/CFT Act; a remote opening is commonly permitted where the ultimate beneficial owner passes enhanced due diligence, the corporate registry extract (Companies Office) is verified electronically, and video identification is accepted. However, most Tier 1 banks require at least one director or the New Zealand-appointed agent to attend an in-person verification at a branch in New Zealand or at a foreign branch of the same banking group. Physical presence interviews are not a statutory mandate per se, but banks may impose them as a contractual condition under their internal AML/CFT customer due diligence policies. The practical default for a fintech hardware entity is: remote onboarding is possible with a New Zealand resident director or registered agent, a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation, register of directors and shareholders, and beneficial ownership declaration, but individual bank policies vary; ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac generally prefer an in-country interview for non-resident-owned entities with significant offshore turnover.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident individual or trust-based holding structure lacking clear economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised passport copies of all natural-person beneficial owners; certified corporate register extracts; full trust deed or trust structure chart showing settlor, trustee, protector and beneficiaries; source-of-wealth declaration supported by bank statements, sale-and-purchase agreement for the original capital, audited financial statements, and a letter from a certified accountant confirming economic substance of the New Zealand entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume anticipated turnover from e-commerce sales of AI robotic hardware without a physical operational footprint in New Zealand
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed distribution and OEM/assembly agreements; product compliance certificates (AS/NZS IEC 60065 or equivalent electrical safety standards); inventory warehousing contract in New Zealand or third-country logistics provider; pro-forma invoices and a 12-month cash-flow forecast; website and marketplace seller-account verification; patent/trademark registration certificates for the AI pet robot; customer contract samples demonstrating genuine commercial transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments mismatch: inbound receivables from Asia and North America with outbound supplier payments to China or South-East Asia for components
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply-chain documentation package including purchase orders, supplier contracts, shipping documents (bill of lading, air waybill), customs entry records, inspection certificates, and transfer-pricing documentation showing arm's-length margins; bank narrative describing the operating cycle; proof of third-party fulfilment and customer delivery addresses; historical bank statements showing consistent correlation between purchases and sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a registered agent rather than a locally resident director or employees; perceived shell company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Listed director's CV and proof of residence; registered-agent services agreement; board resolution appointing the local director with delegated authority to access books and records; New Zealand IRD number registration confirmation; evidence of local business activities such as product sample import, customs clearance, attended trade shows, or regulated-agent premises sharing agreement; statutory declaration from the director confirming active management and control in New Zealand.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency or alternative-payment-source deposits in customer settlement flows (e.g. credit card aggregator settling into the corporate account)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment service provider (Stripe, PayPal) verification reports; settlement reconciliation records linking card transactions to unique order IDs; platform anti-fraud review logs; refund policy; chargeback history report; declaration that no crypto-asset payments are accepted; compliance with card scheme merchant rules and a clean sanctions/PEP screening result.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders may inject equity capital into the New Zealand Limited Company via international SWIFT payment in the shareholder's own name referencing the company name and share-allotment purpose. No Reserve Bank approval or exchange-control permission is required; however, the bank will require the completed 'KYC purpose of payment' field to state clearly 'Capital contribution / Subscription for shares in [Company Name]' and may request a copy of the board resolution authorising the share issue, the register of allotment (Form NZ Companies Office AR), and the shareholders' agreement. Inward payments in any major foreign currency may be credited to a foreign-currency account or converted to NZD at the bank's prevailing FX rate. If the amount exceeds NZD 10,000 in cash (or its equivalent), a 'large cash transaction report' must be filed by the bank under the AML/CFT regime; additionally, any telegraphic transfer over NZD 10,000 is automatically captured by the bank's prescribed transaction reporting system and reported to the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit. Inbound foreign direct investment is screened under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 only if the investor acquires 'sensitive land' or 'significant business assets' (typically more than NZD 100 million turnover); an AI pet robot manufacturer with a standard product-companies register or a special-purpose vehicle will generally not exceed this threshold. Documentary package recommended: capital contribution agreement, board minutes, share register update, source-of-funds evidence (shareholder's bank statement and accumulated-profit financials), and a solicitor's trust account letter where applicable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border trade settlement for component imports and marketing purchases should be executed through the banking-grade SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfer for open-account transactions, and by irrevocable documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700 series) for larger supplier contracts where payment security is required. The Australian and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ), ASB, BNZ, Westpac and HSBC provide direct SWIFT connectivity, electronic banking portals (ANZ Transactive, BNZ Online, Westpac One, HSBCnet), and multi-currency accounts. For outbound remittances exceeding the value threshold, the remitting bank must report the transaction to the Financial Intelligence Unit as a prescribed transaction; typical 'purpose of payment' codes used are under the IMF Balance of Payments classification: 'General trade – goods import' (D-prefixed BOP codes such as D120 for primary income or trade codes assigned by the bank) and each bank's internal reason code mapping applies. Where the New Zealand entity imports electronic components from a related supplier, a transfer-pricing memorandum should evidence the arm's-length price to avoid New Zealand Revenue (Inland Revenue) scrutiny. Payment timing discipline: align disbursements with the LC presentation schedule and bill-of-lading arrival to avoid unnecessary FX conversion costs; use same-day NZD clearing through the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) for domestic legs. Permissible clearing rails also include CLS (Continuous Linked Settlement) for major currency pairs, and bank-to-bank correspondent networks; however, the practical rails are SWIFT MT103 for direct beneficiary settlement, MT700 LC confirmed by a New Zealand bank, and card-scheme settlement via Stripe/acquiring bank for consumer e-commerce revenue.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (outright NZD/USD, NZD/CNH and NZD/EUR forwards) with a registered New Zealand bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a bank-specific FX terms master agreement
FX Swaps (roll-over swaps used to manage working capital across settlement date mismatches)
Cross-Currency Swaps (fixed-floating cross-currency interest-rate swaps for hedging a foreign-currency term loan financing the working-capital cycle)

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on restricted Asian currencies such as CNY/CNH, INR, IDR, PHP or KRW where the underlying exposure is settled in such currencies and the NDF is cash-settled in NZD or USD; permitted for hedging forecast receivables or payables, provided the NDF is transacted with a licensed New Zealand bank or an authorised FX dealer and clearly documented as a hedge of commercial exposure rather than a speculative position
FX Options (plain-vanilla vanillas and put/call options) used to cap adverse currency movement on large discrete trade payments, subject to board approval and derivative risk-management minutes
Money-market and FX spot accelerators (same-day FX conversion and sweep accounts) as a liquidity tool, not a derivative, to minimise conversion cost on regular inbound card settlement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act 1993 ss 212–216) – confirmation of company name, registered office, directors, shareholding, and ultimate beneficial ownership details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Company-specific 'filing month' equal to the anniversary month of incorporation; must be filed online during that calendar month each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Every director commits an offence punishable by a fine of up to NZ$10,000 per section 216; repeated non-filing after Registrar reminder and 20+ working-day notice triggers Gazette Notice of Intention to Remove and administrative strike-off from the New Zealand Companies Register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements in the Full Annual Return (mandatory for companies with 10 or more shareholders, 'large' companies as defined by the Financial Reporting Act 2013, or FMC reporting entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), MBIE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Lodged with the Annual Return within the company's filing month (same anniversary-deadline rule); no separate statutory extension is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Included in the Annual Return filing; failure to attach audited financial statements where required subjects directors to the same personal fines and triggers the same administrative removal process as non-filing of the Annual Return

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is mandatory where (i) total assets exceed NZ$60 million or total revenue exceeds NZ$30 million (large company), (ii) the company has 10 or more shareholders, (iii) the company is an FMC reporting entity (listed issuer, registered bank, or licensed insurer), or (iv) shareholders holding at least 5% of votes request an audit under section 202 of the Companies Act 1993. A private NZ Ltd with fewer than 10 shareholders and below these thresholds is audit-exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ GAAP: Tier 1 – IFRS-converged NZ IFRS; Tier 2 – NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR); Tiers 3 and 4 – Simple Format Reporting (SFR) as prescribed by the External Reporting Board (XRB)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no standalone UBO register. The Annual Return is the statutory annual confirmation instrument: it prepopulates current members, share classes, and 25%+ beneficial holdings, which the directors must verify and update. Share transfers or allotments during the year are recorded in the company's own Share Register and the updated position is confirmed in the next Annual Return; AML/CFT customer due diligence on beneficial owners applies separately where the company is an AML/CFT reporting entity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Preferential reliefs include a refundable R&D tax credit of 15% of eligible R&D expenditure (cash-out cap NZD 255,000 per income year), immediate expensing of low-value depreciable assets (cost thresholds generally NZD 1,000), depreciation deductions on fixed plant and equipment, and the New Zealand imputation credit system, which eliminates economic double taxation on distributed profits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry; carry-forward is subject to the 49% shareholder continuity rule and, where more than a 50% ownership change occurs, the same-business continuity test).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 – Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR Secure Online Services or via approved tax software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return is due 7 July immediately after the income year end. With a tax agent extension, the filing deadline is generally extended to 31 March of the following year. Terminal tax remains payable on 7 February. Non-standard balance dates shift these dates proportionately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part A – Company Identity and IRD Details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal company name, IRD number, registered office address, physical principal place of business, contact details, and balance date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the IRD number allocated to the New Zealand permanent establishment or the non-resident company's New Zealand registration. If no IRD number exists, apply through an authorised New Zealand agent before filing. Do not substitute overseas tax identification numbers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from sales, service revenue, interest, dividends, and other assessable income; allowable business expenses; net taxable profit or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only New Zealand-sourced income and income attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment. Apportion global overheads using documented arm's length methods. Disclose all cross-border related-party transactions and any transfer pricing adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part C – Transfer Pricing and Loss Claims
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate related-party transaction values, transfer pricing election details, loss carry-forward schedules, and imputation credit account entries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZD 1,000,000, maintain and be prepared to attach a contemporaneous transfer pricing report. Claim loss carry-forwards only where statutory continuity requirements are satisfied, and confirm whether any DTA relief requires a current Certificate of Residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part D – Tax Calculation and Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income, income tax liability at 28%, imputation credits, R&D tax credits, resident withholding tax credits, and residual income tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are generally subject to final non-resident withholding tax at source; treaty relief is invoked by the payer holding a valid Certificate of Residence before payment. Any excess New Zealand tax may be claimed by filing an IR4 through myIR.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty NZD 50 per return, with additional reminder penalties up to NZD 500 for persistent non-filing. Late payment penalties commence at 1% of the unpaid tax and may increase by 4% after seven days and by further periodic penalties. Use-of-money interest accrues daily at the IRD prescribed underpayment rate.
